response.headline: Terrain blocking the line to every nearby mast is the likely cause [terrain_blocking].

causes.explanation: 466 people are in cells where terrain blocks the line to every site within 5 km [zone_overview], and new high-ground masts would give clear lines to most poorly served people [cand_1][cand_2][cand_3]; mast heights are assumed, so the margin is uncertain.

1,140 people have no identified site within 5 km [zone_overview], while existing sites are 3.2–5.7 km away [existing_1][existing_2][existing_3]; operator identities for two sites are unknown, so coverage per operator is not confirmed.
Only 5 Ookla tests with low data confidence and no per-cell measurements exist [zone_overview][fix_rule], so the evidence cannot separate terrain from distance or operator-specific gaps.
On average only 0.5 operators have approximate sites within 5 km [zone_overview], but existing sites list EE, Three and Vodafone [existing_1], so a single-operator gap is not proven at the point.

fix_plan.why: Only 5 Ookla tests with low data confidence exist, so terrain and distance gaps cannot be separated [zone_overview][fix_rule]; [cand_1] gives the most poorly served zone residents a clear line (1374 people) once measurements confirm the need [cand_1].
assumptions: line of sight to cell centres, not a radio model
fix_plan.candidate_finding: Candidate 1: a new 25 m mast on high ground (533 m, near the zone) would give 1374 of the zone's people a clear line of sight (1374 poorly served people in all; 3485 people reached in 35 of 49 cells checked).

review.reason: Plan correctly uses the zone's people gaining (1374) from [cand_1] not everyone reached (3485); assumptions are stated; fix_type 'gather_data' matches [fix_rule]'s 'measure first' for a gap zone with weak data; weak data (5 Ookla tests, low confidence) is flagged in why citing [zone_overview] and [fix_rule].

limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level.
